_: Interactive controls with NO ACCESSIBLE NAME, MEASURED on the rendered page. Same ratchet as the touch audits: a number may only go DOWN, and the audit fails if one climbs or if one falls without this file being tightened.
_why: A control with no name fails twice at once. Someone using VoiceOver cannot tell what it does — and no test can address it either, which is how the New Sale product card went a year unnamed and left the exact screen from Ali's screenshot the one screen no audit could open. Three CI rounds were spent guessing at a selector for a control that simply had no name to select it by.
_first_run: MEASURED by CI on 2026-09-03, every baseline provisionally 60 so the run would report the truth rather than have me predict it. The truth was better than expected: 19 of 21 screens already clean, and exactly TWO controls in the whole app with no accessible name — the filter toggle on Products, and the refresh button on My Deliveries. Both icon-only, both 44x44, both announced as 'button' and nothing else. Both named in the same change, so every screen is 0.
_the_expensive_one: The card this audit exists because of is NOT on this list, and that is the point. The New Sale product card is inside a sheet, and a sheet is not a screen — the same blind spot that let a 36px pill sit in front of Ali while every control was reported as 44px. It was named on 2026-09-02 when the touch audit finally reached that step. If this check is ever extended, extend it into the sheets first: that is where the money is entered and where the naming defect actually was.
